recheck: a Claude Code release that changes the transcript format, or a drift run that reports new or vanished keys
basis: collect.py census over 104 sessions on one reference machine (2.1.275-2.1.287), a different population from the spikes that set the thresholds in sweep-rules.json: each key below is on every record of its population in 2.1.284, 2.1.285 and 2.1.287, except effort (99.8%) and turn_duration (30-47% of system records); invariant:usage_split counted 16 groups, all in subagents, none in 2.1.287. key_path:user:entrypoint was added 2026-10-04: it decides which sessions sweep sets aside as automated, and its feeds are the four metrics whose pooled and interactive-only medians the 2026-10-03 audit compared (764 sessions), all of which moved; no other metric was compared, so widen the feeds if a later comparison shows one moving; it was on every user record of headless 2.1.288 sessions, not yet checked over the reference machine's corpus. 2026-10-18: the turn_duration canaries were dropped because time.active_s no longer reads that record (it sums main-session record gaps capped at 300 s, so it feeds from record timestamps); invariant:active_over_wall and invariant:stop_wait_over_sum count a session whose gap-based active time exceeds its wall clock and a Stop summary whose slowest hook exceeds the sum of its hooks, neither of which the definitions allow, so any count flags a broken reading. 2026-10-25: invariant:usage_split was replaced by invariant:usage_regress after a 2.1.296 sweep reported usage_split lost (#6785): records of one message may now differ on input and cache usage, as the API's message_delta usage is cumulative (https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/streaming#event-types, read 2026-10-25), and last-record-wins dedup stays right as long as no earlier record of a message exceeds its last on input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens or cache_creation_input_tokens, which usage_regress counts. 2026-10-28: collect and sweep over 2,387 sessions (665 interactive; Claude Code 2.1.280-2.1.312, 1,123 of them on 2.1.29x) on one reference machine: the stored census holds no invariant:usage_regress, invariant:active_over_wall or invariant:stop_wait_over_sum count on any version, the sweep reported no canary lost over its newest three versions (2.1.310-2.1.312), and tokens.main and tokens.sub had values (290 of 300 2.1.296 sessions with main usage, the other 10 with no assistant message); the census counts only regressions, not how many messages had several records, so that usage_regress held where records differed is inferred from the 2.1.296 sweep that reported usage_split lost
